title: The relative risk of incident coronary heart disease associated with recently stopping the use of beta-blockers
authors: Psaty BM, Koepsell TD, Wagner EH, LoGerfo JP, Inui TS
population: Patients with drug-treated hypertension in a health maintenance organisation: 248 cases with new coronary heart disease and 737 controls free of coronary heart disease; recent stoppers identified from pharmacy records as filling prescriptions too irregularly to be at least 80% compliant
funder: not read: the full text requires a subscription and is absent from PubMed Central.
result: After adjustment for potential confounders, recent stopping of a beta-blocker carried a transient increase in the relative risk of incident coronary heart disease (relative risk 4.5, 95% CI 1.1 to 18.5). The association was specific to beta-blockers and absent for diuretics. The authors propose a withdrawal syndrome as an acute precipitant of angina and myocardial infarction in hypertensive patients without prior coronary disease.
